title: KV eviction investigation and dashboard playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note collects a compact, operational-first playbook for detecting, triaging, and surfacing KV-cache eviction-induced latency regressions. Audience: oncall operators, service owners for serving-runtime, and engineers instrumenting cache heuristics.

Background and problem statement:
- We’ve seen sporadic spikes in tail latency correlated with higher eviction activity in the read/write KV cache used for prefix/prompt reuse. Evictions create more upstream work (recompute KV state, increased model calls) and can surface as 95/99p RTT regressions for small, latency-sensitive requests.
- Goal: define the minimal set of metrics, traces, and dashboard tiles that let an operator reliably identify eviction-driven incidents and take safe mitigations (e.g., increase cache TTL, route traffic to warm pools, roll back prefetch heuristics).

High-level goals and acceptance criteria:
- Detect eviction-driven incidents within 2 minutes with an SLO-aligned synthetic probe.
- Provide a single dashboard with left-to-right investigative flow: global SLI -> eviction signal -> per-host / per-tenant heatmap -> recent traces anchored to evictions.
- Make remediation actions obvious (links to runbook, feature flags, rollout control).

Key metrics (definition + how to compute + sampling/aggregation):
1) cache.evictions.count
   - Description: total number of eviction events emitted by the KV cache process.
   - Unit/aggregation: count per 1m, sum over hosts; tag by host, node_role, tenant.
   - Sampling: emitted synchronously at eviction; low cardinality.
   - Owner: serving-runtime/cache team.

2) cache.hit_ratio.windowed
   - Description: rolling hit ratio over 30s for prefix KV lookups.
   - Unit: percent (0-100).
   - Derivation: hits / (hits + misses) computed per instance then aggregated by weighted average across hosts.
   - Alerting: warn if ratio drops >10pp vs baseline for 5m, critical if ratio < 60% for 3m.

3) per_request.kv_read_latency_p50_p95_p99
   - Description: latency to read KV entries (includes serialization/deserialization).
   - Unit: ms quantiles.
   - Instrumentation: histograms with exponential buckets; optional lightweight sampling for p99.

4) request.path_time_to_first_token_p95_p99
   - Description: end-to-end time-to-first-token for user requests (SLI).
   - Unit: ms quantiles by route/model/tenant.
   - Use-case: correlate with eviction spikes to confirm end-user impact.

5) synthetic.kv_probe_warmth_score
   - Description: a synthetic probe that performs a canonical prefix sequence and measures hit/miss and TTF token.
   - Unit: composite string: {warmth: [0-1], ttf-ms}. Probe cadence: 30s per region/pool.

Span and tracing contract (narrow, actionable):
- Top-level span: serve.request (existing). Add child spans and attributes:
  - span: kv.cache.lookup
    - attributes: kv.lookup_key (hashed), kv.result: hit|miss|evicted, kv.ttl_remaining_ms, kv.size_bytes, kv.node_role, kv.host_id
  - span: kv.cache.evict (fired only on eviction)
    - attributes: kv.eviction_reason (LRU|expired|memory_pressure|policy_change), kv.evicted_key_count, kv.evicted_total_bytes
  - span: kv.repopulate/prefetch (if prefetch path triggered)
    - attributes: prefetch.strategy, prefetch.origin (request|background), prefetch.duration_ms, prefetch.success_count
- Trace sampling guidance: sample all traces that contain kv.cache.evict spans for 24h, otherwise adaptive sample with weight for high-tail requests. Store as high-priority traces for 7d.

Dashboard layout (left-to-right investigative flow):
1) Top row (SLI + global summary)
   - TTF p50/p95/p99 (30m window) + synthetic.kv_probe_ttf p95 (overlay).
   - Total request rate and error rate.
2) Eviction signal row
   - cache.evictions.count (1m heatline) with host/role breakdown micro-widget.
   - cache.hit_ratio.windowed (30s) as sparkline per-tenant small multiples.
3) Per-tenant / per-host heatmap
   - Host x tenant heatmap showing eviction rate normalized by request volume. Color scale anchored to historical baseline.
4) Latency attribution row
   - Per_request.kv_read_latency histograms + request.path_time_to_first_token quantiles with correlation coefficient widget (evictions vs ttf) computed rolling 1h.
5) Trace anchors + examples
   - Latest 20 traces containing kv.cache.evict spans with direct link to trace viewer and prefilled filters.
6) Remediation and runbook links
   - Quick actions: toggle prefetch ff, promote warm pool, temporarily increase TTL (link to infra flag UI).

Alerting guidance and thresholds (operational rules):
- Eviction surge alert (P2): if cache.evictions.count > baseline*5 for 3 consecutive minutes AND ttf.p95 increases > 15% vs baseline -> page oncall.
- Hit ratio deterioration (P1): if cache.hit_ratio.windowed drops > 12pp for 5m across > 3 hosts -> page and auto-create runbook incident.
- Probe fail (P2): synthetic.kv_probe_warmth_score.warmth < 0.5 for 10m -> page oncall and post to #serving-runtime-alerts.
- Trace quota: automatic trace-sampling uplift when eviction surge detected to capture full context.

Investigation recipe (triage steps for first responder):
1) Confirm: open dashboard, check top row SLI (TTF p95/p99) and eviction signal.
2) Scope: look at host x tenant heatmap to find hotspots; use time-range zoom to 10m.
3) Trace check: open trace anchors viewer for a hotspot; confirm kv.cache.evict spans and check kv.eviction_reason attribute.
4) Root cause hypotheses (quick checklist):
   - memory pressure on host -> check host.memory.free, GC events, kube OOMs.
   - policy update -> recent rollout or config change (linked_artifacts / PR timeline).
   - traffic pattern shift (sudden new tenant or burst) -> verify tenant request rate.
   - cold cache due to long TTL change or restart -> correlate with host restarts.
5) Mitigation options (order of preferred actions):
   - short-term: increase TTL for impacted tenant(s) via feature flag or route override.
   - mid-term: shift heavier traffic to dedicated warm pool or replicate key prefixes.
   - long-term: tune eviction policy (adaptive aging) + capacity increase.
6) Post-mortem anchors: record the eviction_count delta, TTF delta, and speculative cause; capture any configuration toggles used as mitigation.

Instrumentation TODO checklist (developer-facing):
- Emit cache.evictions.count with reasons and host tags (PR: PR#4821).
- Add kv.cache.lookup and kv.cache.evict span instrumentation in serving-runtime (lib-level helpers).
- Implement synthetic probe per-pool; expose probe output as metric and event.
- Add high-signal trace sampling rule: include any trace containing kv.cache.evict for 24h.

Query snippets (for quick use in dashboard panels / investigation):
- Eviction spike window: SELECT sum(evictions) FROM metrics WHERE metric='cache.evictions.count' AND timestamp > now()-10m GROUP BY host ORDER BY sum DESC LIMIT 50
- Per-tenant heat: SELECT tenant, sum(evictions)/max(requests,1) as evict_per_kreq FROM metrics WHERE metric in ('cache.evictions.count','request.count') AND timestamp > now()-1h GROUP BY tenant
- Correlation quick: SELECT corr(evictions, ttf_p95) FROM metric_timeseries WHERE window=1h

Open questions and next steps (for coordination):
- How much trace retention cost can central observability tolerate for always-capturing eviction traces? Proposal: store eviction traces at full fidelity for 7d and sampled downwards after that.
- Should synthetic probe cadence be 30s or 60s for global cost tradeoff? Start 30s for warm pools; 60s for regional.
- Owner assignments: cache.evictions.count emitter -> serving-runtime/cache; synthetic probe -> observability team; dashboard assembly -> observability + console.

Notes to self / rough agenda for follow-up meeting:
- Walk the draft with serving-runtime on 2025-03-05, confirm span attribute names.
- Prototype a dashboard widget with host x tenant heatmap and link to PR#4821.
- Prepare runbook stub to convert selected alerts into playbook automations (Slack + PagerDuty).
